## [1] LSST single frame outputs
When running the single_frame task, you're producing a subset of all available HSC datasets for analysis (modeled by the -i flag), and then outputting the results (modeled by the -o flag) in a consistent format.

The output includes the sky coverage dimensions (width, height, and WCS mapping), and the total RA and Dec coverage. These outputs are computed using a variety of input datasets, and thus can produce different results each time the task runs.

Here are a few possibilities for why different outputs may be observed:

1. Different datasets: Each dataset may have slightly different sky coverage, image quality, and other characteristics. Running the task a few times with slightly different input datasets (modeled by -i flag) can lead to different outputs.

2. Differing calibration: The calibration of the telescope and instruments can vary slightly between runs. This can affect how sky coverage is measured, leading to different results.
